alignments.note: Adverb ὅλως → *actually*.
Passive ἀκούεται with its supplied subject *It* and auxiliary *is* riding along under rules 7 and 9; rule 17 heads on the lexical *reported*, not on the expletive or the auxiliary.

The Greek subject noun is expanded into a finite English clause *that there is fornication*; the complementizer, the expletive subject and the copula are rule 7 helpers on the noun that licenses them (rules 85 and 96), headed on the noun.
ἐν → *among*.
ὑμῖν → *you*.
καί → *and*.
Attributive τοιαύτη → *such*; the Greek noun is anarthrous, so no article competes.
πορνεία → *fornication*; split from the demonstrative under rule 26.
Relative ἥτις → *as*.
οὐδέ → *not even*; no second negative word stands, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
The relative clause is verbless with a prepositional predicate, so rule 53 gives the supplied copula *is* to the preposition; discontinuous under rule 15, headed on *among*.
Article → *the* under rule 19.
ἔθνεσιν → *Gentiles*.
ὥστε introduces the English clause and takes *that* under rule 40; the infinitive is rendered finite.
τινα → *one*.

The italicized partitive *of you* is licensed by no source token: τις is already complete as *one*, and ὑμῖν has been spent on t010, so rule 103 marks it added rather than folding it under rule 7. Reading it as a rule 7 completion of τινα remains defensible.
ἔχειν → *hath*, the conjunction having taken the clause-introducer.

The possessor stands before the head noun in English, so under rule 57 the genitive's own article takes the determiner the ASV writes on the possessor — *his* — exactly as τὸ τοῦ ἑτέρου → *his neighbor's good*.
πατρός takes only the possessive word *father's* under rule 57.
γυναῖκα → *wife*; the determiner slot is occupied by the English possessive phrase.

review_notes: The supplied *that there is* is folded onto πορνεία rather than onto ἀκούεται, because the clause it introduces is the noun's own expansion (rules 85, 96).
*of you* is marked added under rule 103; the ASV italicizes it, which rule 11 treats as corroborating evidence.
